Looking at the [Current sources:](https://github.com/CivicActions/allusgov).

These are APIs so if the endpoint breaks or it doesn't return results this shouldn't need to be updated to draw new data:

- https://open.gsa.gov/api/fh-public-api/
- https://www.federalregister.gov/developers/documentation/api/v1#/Agencies
- https://api.usaspending.gov/

I guess this needs to be scraped:
https://www.usa.gov/agency-index

But it should be the same as this info here, right? 

https://www.opm.gov/about-us/open-government/Data/Apps/Agencies/

**Can just be downloaded with a script on a monthly basis:**

https://www.opm.gov/about-us/open-government/Data/Apps/agencies/agencies.xml


We could probably learn some things from the zone file, from here:
https://github.com/cisagov/dotgov-data?tab=readme-ov-file

**I think we just need the full or federal list, which can be downloaded with a script on a monthly basis:**
https://github.com/cisagov/dotgov-data/blob/main/current-full.csv
https://github.com/cisagov/dotgov-data/blob/main/current-federal.csv


Ultimately it seems that annually (in mid March) we'd need to search in GovInfo:

And instead of looking for:
https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/BUDGET-2024-DB/BUDGET-2024-DB-2

We'd need to use:
https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/BUDGET-2025-DB/BUDGET-2025-DB-2

Or alternatively, just download once a year with a year variable? It might work going ahead:

https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/BUDGET-$year-DB/BUDGET-$year-DB-2

Not sure if that would work.

I suspect we'd need to **check out what is on offer here as it isn't consistent.**

Took a look and I don't _think_ this relates to the org structure - perhaps I missed something though?

`uv run mypy allusgov/processor` didn't return any issues for me.
```
$ uv run mypy allusgov/processor/normalize_name.py 
Success: no issues found in 1 source file
```
 
It looks like I need to run this instead:
```
uv run mypy allusgov/processor/normalize_name.py --disallow-untyped-defs
```

I added focused regression assertions for source provenance in the text, flat JSON, and CSV exports. I've kept this as a draft because native tests haven't run yet. The current Tests & Analysis workflow shows `action_required` and zero jobs; if the project permits running CI for fork PRs, would approval of that workflow be possible when convenient? I'm happy to address any failures. If this is expected under your contribution policy, no action needed.
